newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ford studies tiny car for India, China markets.
newsitem.headline: Ford studies tiny car for India, China markets.

text.p: Ford Motor Co chairman Alex Trotman said the company was studying the possibility of building a car even lighter and less expensive than its new Ka minicar for the Indian and Chinese markets.

"It would have a cost and weight below the Fiesta and Ka...but we haven't taken a decision to proceed with a major investment," Trotman told a luncheon at the Paris car show. "We're very aggressive in increasing our presence in developing countries. Growth in the next century will come from Asia and South America with almost stable growth in Europe and North America," he said.

Ford recently began producing a European version of the Escort at a plant in Bombay, it will produce Fiestas in Madras, it has five joint ventures in China and projects in Thailand, Vietnam and Egypt.
The company is building a plant in Poland, plans to set up production in Belarus and is studying production in Russia.
Trotman said the car under study, which would be aimed at the Chinese and Indian markets, would be "extremely low-cost, very simple in design and very durable".
